description: The plot illustrates how Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) varies with the number of child nodes (tree width) for two models. The x-axis is labeled “Num. of Child Nodes (Tree Width)” on a linear scale with values shown at 1, 3, 5, and 7 (tick interval 2). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy@1 (%)” on a linear scale spanning roughly 15% to 38%, with labeled ticks at 15, 20, 25, 30, and 35 (tick interval 5 percentage points). One line represents GPT-4o as a darker blue solid line with circular markers; it starts at 24.4% at tree width 1, rises to 28.9% at 3, increases to 34.4% at 5, then decreases to 31.1% at 7. The other line represents Claude-3.5-Sonnet as a lighter blue solid line with “x” markers; it starts at 26.7% at tree width 1, increases to 27.8% at 3, then declines to 24.4% at 5 and further declines to 20.0% at 7.
caption_used: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (RIGHT) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with GPT-4o peaking at 31.1% and Claude-3.5-Sonnet consistently outperforming GPT-4o across all tree widths.
